Check a rating from the flow record

Source: R/check_flow_record.R
check_flow_record.Rd

Archived flow is stage passed through whichever rating was applied at the time, so the archived pairs of stage and flow carry that rating. check_flow_record() reads it back, period by period, and checks it for what gaugings cannot show: when it changed, where the record departs from it, how much flow came from above its top, and how far a stage error moves the flow. It fits nothing, never edits the record, and never sets a number the caller did not give: a check whose input is missing is reported as not assessed, with the reason.

The method, its failure behaviour and its limitations are set out in design/E3_record_checks.md.

Usage

check_flow_record(
  record,
  top_stage_m = NULL,
  bankfull_stage_m = NULL,
  stage_uncertainty_m = NULL,
  dry = NULL,
  ratings = NULL,
  tolerance = 0.01,
  abs_tolerance = 0.002,
  stage_resolution_m = 0.001,
  max_gap_m = 0.01,
  min_days = 2L,
  off_curve_share = 0.01,
  above_top_share = 0.05,
  known_fit_share = 0.05,
  dry_rise_m_per_day = 0.001,
  min_period_steps = 100L
)

Arguments

record

A data frame or data.table, one row per step, with time (POSIXct, UTC, the step's start), stage_m (metres above the gauge datum), discharge_cms (archived flow, m3/s) and, optionally, quality (the archive's quality code for the flow). Times must increase, by whole multiples of the shortest step; a gap is a run of missing steps.

top_stage_m

The highest stage the rating is founded on: the highest gauging, or the stated limit of its top limb. Enables record_above_top.

bankfull_stage_m

The stage above which water may bypass the section. Enables record_above_bankfull.

stage_uncertainty_m

A stage error, as a systematic offset in metres. Enables record_stage_error.

dry

Logical, one per row of record: TRUE where the caller judges no rain has fallen on the catchment long enough to matter. Enables record_dry_rises. On a permeable catchment, flow can go on rising for days after rain as the groundwater answers it: weed grows in summer, so a rise in a winter month is more likely the catchment than the channel.

ratings

Known ratings: a named list of FlodeRating or FlodeRatingTable, or the output of operational_rating_tables(). Enables record_known_ratings.

tolerance, abs_tolerance

A step departs from the curve by more than max(tolerance * C, abs_tolerance). Defaults 1% and 0.002 m3/s: flow stored to three decimals is 1% out from rounding alone at 0.05 m3/s.

stage_resolution_m

The resolution stage is archived to.

max_gap_m

The widest gap between curve stages a step may be interpolated across.

min_days

Departing days in a row that make a revision.

off_curve_share

Share of a period's flow volume off the curve above which record_off_curve warns.

above_top_share

Share of flow volume above top_stage_m above which record_above_top warns.

known_fit_share

Share of a period's steps that may depart from a known rating for it still to fit.

dry_rise_m_per_day

The mean rise of stage over a month's dry steps, metres a day, above which record_dry_rises warns.

min_period_steps

A period with fewer tested steps is listed but not assessed.

Value

A list of class flode_record_check:

assessment

A FlodeAssessment, one row per check.

periods

One row per period: period, start, end, steps, tested, stage_min_m, stage_max_m, assessed, and the known rating matched, where ratings is given.

curves

A list of data.tables (stage_m, discharge_cms), one per period: the rating read back.

revisions

One row per revision: time, from_period, to_period, kind ("stage shift" or "change of shape"), shift_m, flow_change (at the new period's median stage, as a fraction).

off_curve

One row per run of departing steps: period, start, end, steps, volume_share, quality.

above

Peaks above the top and bankfull stages: limit, start, end, peak_time, peak_stage_m, peak_discharge_cms; with the shares of volume in attribute shares.

stage_error

By year and flow band: the volume change from the offset raised and lowered, m3 and as a share.

dry_rises

By month: dry steps, mean stage change and flow change a day.

steps

The record with period, curve_cms, tested and departs added.

counts

Steps in, missing stage, missing flow, tested, untested.

settings

Every argument, as used.

Details

The thresholds are best-endeavours defaults, not EA policy (limitation L02).

How the rating is read back

An applied rating is exact: the archived flow at a stage is the rating's flow there, less rounding. A step departs when |Q - C(h)| > max(tolerance * C(h), abs_tolerance), with C the curve read back for the step's period. The curve is, at each distinct stage (to stage_resolution_m), the median flow recorded there, linearly interpolated between stages at most max_gap_m apart. A step at a stage the period has not yet seen is untested; nothing is extrapolated.

The record is read a day at a time. A day departs when more than half its tested steps depart. A departing day followed by departing days, making min_days in a row, closes the period: a revision, dated at the first departing step of the first such day. Shorter runs are reported as off the curve. Each revision is classed as a stage shift of d metres when the new curve is the old one moved by d (C_new(h) = C_old(h + d) at 95% of the stages both cover), or a change of shape otherwise.

See also

compare_gaugings_to_rating(), which tests a rating against gaugings: the record shows the rating as applied, the gaugings whether it is right.

Examples

# A year of a known rating, Q = 5 (h - 0.1)^1.6, with a revision part way:
# from 1 July the flow is the same rating read 0.05 m higher.
time <- seq(as.POSIXct("2024-01-01", tz = "UTC"), by = 900, length.out = 35136)
stage <- round(0.45 + 0.25 * sin(2 * pi * seq_along(time) / 672), 3)
shifted <- time >= as.POSIXct("2024-07-01", tz = "UTC")
flow <- round(5 * (stage + 0.05 * shifted - 0.1)^1.6, 3)
out <- check_flow_record(data.frame(time = time, stage_m = stage, discharge_cms = flow))
out$revisions
#>          time from_period to_period        kind shift_m flow_change
#>        <POSc>       <int>     <int>      <char>   <num>       <num>
#> 1: 2024-07-01           1         2 stage shift    0.05   0.2337526
assessment_checks(out$assessment)[, .(check_id, status)]
#>                 check_id       status
#>                   <char>       <char>
#> 1:         record_tested         pass
#> 2:      record_revisions      warning
#> 3:      record_off_curve         pass
#> 4:      record_above_top not_assessed
#> 5: record_above_bankfull not_assessed
#> 6:    record_stage_error not_assessed
#> 7:      record_dry_rises not_assessed
#> 8:  record_known_ratings not_assessed
